Adblue, as Thomas Morell writes, is a reducing agent used in selective catalytic reduction to reduce emissions of nitrogen oxides, so-called SCR catalyst. Without administration of Adblue, the SCR catalyst is damaged and the emissions of nitrogen oxides from combustion are then released straight into the air. The SCR system is now a common technology in combustion plants and in larger ships but also in diesel-powered road vehicles, such as buses, trucks and passenger cars. If SCR systems were disconnected from installations and vehicles, emissions would thus increase, with major adverse health effects and thus significant societal costs. In this situation, Sweden would also have major problems meeting the requirements of the EU's air quality and air pollution directives, with the risk of high periodic penalty payments being imposed.
